html:
SMTO-ART-0018 — Saving a file was stopped before it finished

GUID: f80a7457-5196-4dfd-835d-5b00c046e517
Slug: artifact-cancelled
Domain: ART · Subsystem: art

What happened

  • SMTO was saving a file from this Task when the save was cancelled, usually because the Task or one of its steps was stopped. Some files may have been saved before that.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Artifacts from this run and note which files are listed with a Download link. Files saved before the stop are kept, so you only need to redo the missing ones.
  2. If the list shows files still waiting, select Retry collection once. Collection picks up finished files the Task left behind without running its commands again.
  3. If a file is still missing because the Task was stopped before making it, ask SMTO in a new message to create that file. A stopped Task may never have finished writing that file, so it needs to be made again.

What success looks like

  • Every file you need appears once in Artifacts from this run.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before trying it again: look in Artifacts from this run first. Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't start the whole Task again before checking the list; that can repeat commands that already ran.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Artifact registration or materialization saw its cancellation event during chunk reads, staging or the final publication check and abandoned the new version.

What this means

  • Artifact registration/materialization observes its cancellation event during read, staging or final publication checks. Artifact publication and presentation remain separate from the command that produced a file. Only an explicit pre-dispatch rejection proves that new command did not run; diagnostics do not collect, transfer, quarantine or delete files.

Why this can happen

  • Artifact registration/materialization observes its cancellation event during read, staging or final publication checks.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect cancellation provenance, original registration/transfer stage and retained source bytes.

How to fix it

  • Check why the operation's cancel_event was set (Task stop, interrupt or timeout) in the run trace, then inspect registered_artifacts and the run's artifact_collection state to see what was already published. Use the run's artifacts reconcile endpoint (Retry collection), which collects finalized outputs without cancellation, instead of re-running the producing tool.
  • Inspect cancellation provenance and any retained source or partial transfer before requesting new collection.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • The original partial/publication state is known before any deliberate new collection.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • Artifact publication and presentation remain separate from the command that produced a file. Only an explicit pre-dispatch rejection proves that new command did not run; diagnostics do not collect, transfer, quarantine or delete files.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-EXE-0004 — Execution outcome is unknown
